steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 좋은 면: "It helps people stay in touch." (사람들이 계속 연락하고 지내게 도와줘요., 보통); "You can find your community." (나랑 맞는 모임을 찾을 수 있어요., 보통); "It has its uses." (나름 쓸모가 있어요., 친근)
- 나쁜 면: "Everyone shows only their best moments." (다들 가장 좋은 순간만 보여 줘요., 보통); "It’s easy to compare yourself." (나를 남과 비교하기 쉬워요., 보통); "It’s designed to be addictive." (중독되게 설계돼 있어요., 보통)
- 내 습관: "I spend too much time scrolling." (화면을 넘기며 시간을 너무 많이 써요., 친근); "I took a break from it once." (한 번 쉬어 본 적이 있어요., 친근); "It’s how you use it." (어떻게 쓰느냐가 중요해요., 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 피드 이야기 낱말

*visible* 눈에 보이는 · *visual* 시각적인(그림·사진의) 
*intense* 강렬한, 심한 · *ruin* your mood 기분을 망치다 
*get rid of* 없애다 · Comments can *get ugly*. 댓글이 험해질 수 있어요.
(참고) 볼 수 있는 낱말

*violent* 폭력적인 · *divorce* 이혼(법적으로 결혼을 끝내는 것) 
일반적인 의견이에요. 건강 조언이 아니에요.

A: At the same ___, it makes people ___ left out.   B: True. It’s how you ___ it. 
낱말 상자: doubt · time · feel · use
steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 피드 이야기 낱말: visible 눈에 보이는 · visual 시각적인(그림·사진의) / intense 강렬한, 심한 · ruin your mood 기분을 망치다 / get rid of 없애다 · Comments can get ugly. 댓글이 험해질 수 있어요.
- (참고) 볼 수 있는 낱말: violent 폭력적인 · divorce 이혼(법적으로 결혼을 끝내는 것) / 일반적인 의견이에요. 건강 조언이 아니에요.
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: Does social media make you happy? B: There’s no ___ that it helps me stay in touch. / A: At the same ___, it makes people ___ left out. B: True. It’s how you ___ it. / 낱말 상자: doubt · time · feel · use
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.

Picture words on screen. New: scroll ((화면을) 넘기다, 스크롤하다), filter ((사진) 필터), profile (프로필(나를 소개하는 페이지)), influencer (인플루언서), content (콘텐츠(글·영상·사진)), algorithm (알고리즘(보여 줄 것을 고르는 규칙)), connect (연결하다, 이어지다), envy (부러움, 시기), comparison (비교), self-esteem (자존감), mental (정신의, 마음의), design (설계하다, 디자인하다).
Go through about six, new ones first: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and let the learner say it. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: social (사회의, 사람들과 어울리는) — "social media"; media (매체, 미디어) — "She works in media."; compare (비교하다) — "Don’t compare yourself."; community (공동체, 모임) — "an online community"; addictive (중독성 있는) — "Short videos are addictive."; break (휴식, 잠깐 쉬기) — "a break from my phone"; platform (플랫폼(공유하는 사이트·앱)) — "a video platform"; surprisingly (놀랍게도, 뜻밖에) — "Surprisingly, I didn’t miss it.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Which apps or sites do people around you use most?
Most people I know use ___ apps.
What is one good thing about social media?
What can make people feel bad online?
Give one good point and one bad point about short videos.
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Which apps or sites do people around you use most?" (hint on screen: Most people I know use ___ apps.)
- "What is one good thing about social media?" (hint on screen: There’s no doubt that it ___.)
- "What can make people feel bad online?" (hint on screen: ___ makes people feel ___.)
- "Give one good point and one bad point about short videos." (hint on screen: They’re ___. At the same time, ___.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: A Weekend Off
steps.text: That night, Chloe looked at her profile. She had posted lots of content, but she couldn’t remember most of it. She decided to try Jiwoo’s idea, *for the moment* just for the weekend. She turned off alerts and checked messages one app *at a time*. Twice she reached for her phone, then *broke off* and picked up a book. *In the meantime*, she called her mom in Toronto instead of sending emojis. Surprisingly, the call made her laugh more than any post. On Monday, she texted Jiwoo, “I didn’t miss the algorithm at all. But I’ll keep my video makers’ group. It has its uses.” Jiwoo replied, “Nice! Keep the people, get rid of the endless scrolling.”
steps.gloss: for the moment 당분간, 일단 · at a time 한 번에 하나씩 · break off 갑자기 멈추다 · in the meantime 그동안 · surprisingly 놀랍게도 · get rid of 없애다
questions: What did Chloe do instead of sending emojis?
What will Chloe keep, and why?

steps.title: 일회용품 줄이기
steps.title_en: Small changes can make a difference.
steps.scene_desc: 11월 초 목요일 저녁 7시 30분, 동네 카페 안쪽 방. 대니얼이 서서 모임을 진행하며 손에 든 다회용 머그컵을 들어 보이고, 지우가 가방에서 텀블러를 꺼내 웃으며 보여 줌. 탁자에 이웃 몇 명이 둘러앉아 있고, 계산대 옆 선반에 깨끗한 머그컵이 줄지어 있음(간판·안내판에 글자 없이)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Small changes can make a difference." (일회용품 줄이기). Goal: 현실성을 따지며 작은 실천 말하기. Today's scene: 11월 초 목요일 저녁 7시 30분, 동네 카페 안쪽 방. 대니얼이 서서 모임을 진행하며 손에 든 다회용 머그컵을 들어 보이고, 지우가 가방에서 텀블러를 꺼내 웃으며 보여 줌. 탁자에 이웃 몇 명이 둘러앉아 있고, 계산대 옆 선반에 깨끗한 머그컵이 줄지어 있음(간판·안내판에 글자 없이). Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "We should cut down on ___.".

steps.when: 무언가를 덜 쓰자고 제안해요. *cut down on* + 명사 또는 -ing.
steps.extra: We should cut down on paper cups.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "We should cut down on ___." (~을 줄여야 해요.). When to use it: 무언가를 덜 쓰자고 제안해요. cut down on + 명사 또는 -ing. Note: We should cut down on paper cups.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "It’s not realistic to ___.".

steps.when: 좋은 생각이지만 지금 하기엔 너무 어렵다고 말해요.
steps.extra: It’s not realistic to give up plastic completely.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "It’s not realistic to ___." (~하는 건 현실적이지 않아요.). When to use it: 좋은 생각이지만 지금 하기엔 너무 어렵다고 말해요. Note: It’s not realistic to give up plastic completely.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Small changes can make a difference.".

steps.en: Small changes can make a difference.
steps.ko: 작은 변화도 차이를 만들 수 있어요.
steps.when: 작은 것부터 시작하자고 격려해요.
steps.extra: Bring your own cup. Small changes can make a difference.
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "Small changes can make a difference." (작은 변화도 차이를 만들 수 있어요.). When to use it: 작은 것부터 시작하자고 격려해요. Note: Bring your own cup. Small changes can make a difference.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Paper or Mug? · 11월 초, 카페 안쪽 방의 토론 모임에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: Paper or Mug? · 11월 초, 카페 안쪽 방의 토론 모임에서

lines.en: Welcome, everyone. Tonight’s topic is right here. Our café now gives a discount if you bring your own cup. Jiwoo?
lines.ko: 여러분, 어서 오세요. 오늘 주제는 바로 여기 있어요. 이 카페가 이제 개인 컵을 가져오면 할인해 줘요. 지우 씨?

lines.en: I love it. {{I bring my own cup}} most days. {{We should cut down on}} disposable cups.
lines.ko: 정말 좋아요. 저는 거의 매일 제 컵을 가지고 다녀요. 일회용 컵을 줄여야 해요.

lines.en: But are cups the real problem? {{Delivery food comes with so much plastic.}}
lines.ko: 그런데 컵이 진짜 문제일까요? 배달 음식에는 플라스틱이 엄청 많이 딸려 오잖아요.

lines.en: True. That’s why {{companies should take responsibility,}} too.
lines.ko: 맞아요. 그래서 기업도 책임을 져야 해요.

lines.en: Some people say, “Just recycle it.”
lines.ko: ‘그냥 재활용하면 되지’라고 말하는 사람들도 있어요.

lines.en: {{Recycling isn’t enough.}} A lot of it goes in the wrong bin.
lines.ko: 재활용만으로는 부족해요. 많은 양이 엉뚱한 통에 들어가거든요.

lines.en: Let me play devil’s advocate. {{It’s not realistic to}} give up plastic completely. And {{some bans went too far.}}
lines.ko: 일부러 반대로 말해 볼게요. 플라스틱을 완전히 끊는 건 현실적이지 않아요. 지나친 금지도 있었고요.

lines.en: Maybe. {{It’s inconvenient at first.}} But after a while, you don’t even think about it. {{It’s a habit thing.}}
lines.ko: 그럴 수도 있죠. 처음엔 불편해요. 하지만 좀 지나면 생각도 안 하게 돼요. 습관 문제예요.

lines.en: Can you think of an example?
lines.ko: 예가 떠오르는 게 있어요?

lines.en: Me! I forgot my cup every day in March. Now it’s always in my bag.
lines.ko: 저요! 3월에는 매일 컵을 깜빡했어요. 지금은 늘 가방에 있어요.

lines.en: Fair enough. So what can one person really do?
lines.ko: 그렇군요. 그럼 한 사람이 실제로 뭘 할 수 있을까요?

lines.en: {{Small changes can make a difference.}} {{Every little bit helps.}} And {{we can’t just leave it to others.}}
lines.ko: 작은 변화도 차이를 만들 수 있어요. 작은 것 하나하나가 도움이 돼요. 그리고 남한테만 맡겨 둘 수는 없잖아요.

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Paper or Mug? · 11월 초, 카페 안쪽 방의 토론 모임에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Daniel: "Welcome, everyone. Tonight’s topic is right here. Our café now gives a discount if you bring your own cup. Jiwoo?" (여러분, 어서 오세요. 오늘 주제는 바로 여기 있어요. 이 카페가 이제 개인 컵을 가져오면 할인해 줘요. 지우 씨?)
2. Jiwoo: "I love it. I bring my own cup most days. We should cut down on disposable cups." (정말 좋아요. 저는 거의 매일 제 컵을 가지고 다녀요. 일회용 컵을 줄여야 해요.)
3. Daniel: "But are cups the real problem? Delivery food comes with so much plastic." (그런데 컵이 진짜 문제일까요? 배달 음식에는 플라스틱이 엄청 많이 딸려 오잖아요.)
4. Jiwoo: "True. That’s why companies should take responsibility, too." (맞아요. 그래서 기업도 책임을 져야 해요.)
5. Daniel: "Some people say, “Just recycle it.”" (‘그냥 재활용하면 되지’라고 말하는 사람들도 있어요.)
6. Jiwoo: "Recycling isn’t enough. A lot of it goes in the wrong bin." (재활용만으로는 부족해요. 많은 양이 엉뚱한 통에 들어가거든요.)
7. Daniel: "Let me play devil’s advocate. It’s not realistic to give up plastic completely. And some bans went too far." (일부러 반대로 말해 볼게요. 플라스틱을 완전히 끊는 건 현실적이지 않아요. 지나친 금지도 있었고요.)
8. Jiwoo: "Maybe. It’s inconvenient at first. But after a while, you don’t even think about it. It’s a habit thing." (그럴 수도 있죠. 처음엔 불편해요. 하지만 좀 지나면 생각도 안 하게 돼요. 습관 문제예요.)
9. Daniel: "Can you think of an example?" (예가 떠오르는 게 있어요?)
10. Jiwoo: "Me! I forgot my cup every day in March. Now it’s always in my bag." (저요! 3월에는 매일 컵을 깜빡했어요. 지금은 늘 가방에 있어요.)
11. Daniel: "Fair enough. So what can one person really do?" (그렇군요. 그럼 한 사람이 실제로 뭘 할 수 있을까요?)
12. Jiwoo: "Small changes can make a difference. Every little bit helps. And we can’t just leave it to others." (작은 변화도 차이를 만들 수 있어요. 작은 것 하나하나가 도움이 돼요. 그리고 남한테만 맡겨 둘 수는 없잖아요.)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

8. Jiwoo (learner): "Maybe. It’s inconvenient at first. But after a while, you don’t even think about it. It’s a habit thing." (그럴 수도 있죠. 처음엔 불편해요. 하지만 좀 지나면 생각도 안 하게 돼요. 습관 문제예요.)
9. Daniel (you): "Can you think of an example?" (예가 떠오르는 게 있어요?)
10. Jiwoo (learner): "Me! I forgot my cup every day in March. Now it’s always in my bag." (저요! 3월에는 매일 컵을 깜빡했어요. 지금은 늘 가방에 있어요.)
11. Daniel (you): "Fair enough. So what can one person really do?" (그렇군요. 그럼 한 사람이 실제로 뭘 할 수 있을까요?)
12. Jiwoo (learner): "Small changes can make a difference. Every little bit helps. And we can’t just leave it to others." (작은 변화도 차이를 만들 수 있어요. 작은 것 하나하나가 도움이 돼요. 그리고 남한테만 맡겨 둘 수는 없잖아요.)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Daniel. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

items: The café gives a discount for bringing your own cup.
Jiwoo always remembered her cup in March.
steps.teach:
True/false check. The statements on the learner's screen:
1. The café gives a discount for bringing your own cup.
2. Jiwoo thinks recycling is enough.
3. Jiwoo always remembered her cup in March.
The scene they are about:
1. Daniel: "Welcome, everyone. Tonight’s topic is right here. Our café now gives a discount if you bring your own cup. Jiwoo?" (여러분, 어서 오세요. 오늘 주제는 바로 여기 있어요. 이 카페가 이제 개인 컵을 가져오면 할인해 줘요. 지우 씨?)
2. Jiwoo: "I love it. I bring my own cup most days. We should cut down on disposable cups." (정말 좋아요. 저는 거의 매일 제 컵을 가지고 다녀요. 일회용 컵을 줄여야 해요.)
3. Daniel: "But are cups the real problem? Delivery food comes with so much plastic." (그런데 컵이 진짜 문제일까요? 배달 음식에는 플라스틱이 엄청 많이 딸려 오잖아요.)
4. Jiwoo: "True. That’s why companies should take responsibility, too." (맞아요. 그래서 기업도 책임을 져야 해요.)
5. Daniel: "Some people say, “Just recycle it.”" (‘그냥 재활용하면 되지’라고 말하는 사람들도 있어요.)
6. Jiwoo: "Recycling isn’t enough. A lot of it goes in the wrong bin." (재활용만으로는 부족해요. 많은 양이 엉뚱한 통에 들어가거든요.)
7. Daniel: "Let me play devil’s advocate. It’s not realistic to give up plastic completely. And some bans went too far." (일부러 반대로 말해 볼게요. 플라스틱을 완전히 끊는 건 현실적이지 않아요. 지나친 금지도 있었고요.)
8. Jiwoo: "Maybe. It’s inconvenient at first. But after a while, you don’t even think about it. It’s a habit thing." (그럴 수도 있죠. 처음엔 불편해요. 하지만 좀 지나면 생각도 안 하게 돼요. 습관 문제예요.)
9. Daniel: "Can you think of an example?" (예가 떠오르는 게 있어요?)
10. Jiwoo: "Me! I forgot my cup every day in March. Now it’s always in my bag." (저요! 3월에는 매일 컵을 깜빡했어요. 지금은 늘 가방에 있어요.)
11. Daniel: "Fair enough. So what can one person really do?" (그렇군요. 그럼 한 사람이 실제로 뭘 할 수 있을까요?)
12. Jiwoo: "Small changes can make a difference. Every little bit helps. And we can’t just leave it to others." (작은 변화도 차이를 만들 수 있어요. 작은 것 하나하나가 도움이 돼요. 그리고 남한테만 맡겨 둘 수는 없잖아요.)
Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

frame: It’s not realistic to ___. / Small changes can make a difference.
head: We should cut down on …
It’s not realistic to …
But we can …
rows: switch off lights we don’t need.
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: We should cut down on ___. / It’s not realistic to ___. / Small changes can make a difference. Table (We should cut down on … → It’s not realistic to …):
- paper cups. → ban them all at once.
- plastic bags. → stop shopping.
- delivery packaging. → never order food.
- electricity. → turn everything off.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
We should *cut down on* plastic. 플라스틱을 줄여야 해요. 
I’m *cutting down on* ordering delivery. 배달 주문을 줄이고 있어요. (+ -ing) 
I *cut down on* coffee last year. (과거도 cut)

*It’s not realistic to* stop using plastic. 플라스틱을 안 쓰는 건 현실적이지 않아요. 
— 좋은 생각이지만 지금은 너무 어렵다는 뜻 
더 부드럽게: It might not be realistic to …
errors: We should cut down plastic cups.
We should cut down on plastic cups.
It’s not realistic stop using plastic.
It’s not realistic to stop using plastic.
Small changes can make a difference.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- cut down on + 명사 / -ing: We should cut down on plastic. 플라스틱을 줄여야 해요. / I’m cutting down on ordering delivery. 배달 주문을 줄이고 있어요. (+ -ing) / I cut down on coffee last year. (과거도 cut)
- It’s not realistic to + 동사원형: It’s not realistic to stop using plastic. 플라스틱을 안 쓰는 건 현실적이지 않아요. / — 좋은 생각이지만 지금은 너무 어렵다는 뜻 / 더 부드럽게: It might not be realistic to …
Common mistakes on screen:
- We should cut down plastic cups. → We should cut down on plastic cups. (on을 빼지 않아요.)
- It’s not realistic stop using plastic. → It’s not realistic to stop using plastic. (to + 동사원형을 넣어요.)
- Small changes can make difference. → Small changes can make a difference. (a difference라고 해요.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.
points: cut down on + 명사 / -ing: We should cut down on plastic. 플라스틱을 줄여야 해요. I’m cutting down on ordering delivery. 배달 주문을 줄이고 있어요. (+ -ing) I cut down on coffee last year. (과거도 cut)
It’s not realistic to + 동사원형: It’s not realistic to stop using plastic. 플라스틱을 안 쓰는 건 현실적이지 않아요. — 좋은 생각이지만 지금은 너무 어렵다는 뜻 더 부드럽게: It might not be realistic to …
mistakes: We should cut down plastic cups. → We should cut down on plastic cups.
It’s not realistic stop using plastic. → It’s not realistic to stop using plastic.
Small changes can make difference. → Small changes can make a difference.

steps.note: 예) paper cups / ban them all at once → We should cut down on paper cups. But it’s not realistic to ban them all at once.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) paper cups / ban them all at once → We should cut down on paper cups. But it’s not realistic to ban them all at once. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: paper cups → ban them all at once | plastic bags → stop shopping | delivery food → never order it | electricity → turn everything off.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

cards: Small changes can make a difference.
steps.teach:
This is the start of session 2 of "Small changes can make a difference." (일회용품 줄이기); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "We should cut down on ___." / "It’s not realistic to ___." / "Small changes can make a difference.". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: Delivery food comes with so much plastic.
배달 음식엔 플라스틱이 너무 많이 딸려 와요.
We can’t just leave it to others.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 내가 하는 일: "I bring my own cup." (제 컵을 가지고 다녀요., 친근); "It’s inconvenient at first." (처음엔 불편해요., 보통); "It’s a habit thing." (습관 문제예요., 친근); "Every little bit helps." (작은 것 하나하나가 도움이 돼요., 친근)
- 더 큰 그림: "Delivery food comes with so much plastic." (배달 음식엔 플라스틱이 너무 많이 딸려 와요., 보통); "Companies should take responsibility." (기업이 책임을 져야 해요., 보통); "Recycling isn’t enough." (재활용만으로는 부족해요., 보통); "Some bans went too far." (어떤 금지 규정은 너무 지나쳤어요., 보통); "We can’t just leave it to others." (남한테만 맡겨 둘 수는 없어요., 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 변화 이야기 낱말

*tackle* a problem 문제 해결에 나서다 · *rapid* 빠른 
*dramatically* 크게, 급격히 · a *mere* 500 won 고작 500원 
environmental *protection* 환경 보호 
*destruction* 파괴 · *beneath* ~ 아래에
(참고) 낱말 더 보기

a *supplement* 보충(하는 것) · an *amendment* (법·규칙의) 개정 
a *compound* 혼합물, 화합물 · *situated* (~에) 위치한
steps.blank:
A: We should cut ___ on paper cups.   B: Yes, but it’s not ___ to ban them all at once. 
A: True. Small changes can make a ___.   B: Right. Every little bit ___. 
낱말 상자: down · realistic · difference · helps
steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 변화 이야기 낱말: tackle a problem 문제 해결에 나서다 · rapid 빠른 / dramatically 크게, 급격히 · a mere 500 won 고작 500원 / environmental protection 환경 보호 / destruction 파괴 · beneath ~ 아래에
- (참고) 낱말 더 보기: a supplement 보충(하는 것) · an amendment (법·규칙의) 개정 / a compound 혼합물, 화합물 · situated (~에) 위치한
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: We should cut ___ on paper cups. B: Yes, but it’s not ___ to ban them all at once. / A: True. Small changes can make a ___. B: Right. Every little bit ___. / 낱말 상자: down · realistic · difference · helps
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: plastic (플라스틱), disposable (일회용의), reusable (다시 쓸 수 있는), recycle (재활용하다), pollution (오염), planet (행성; (the planet) 지구), chemical (화학 물질), fuel (연료), metal (금속), climate (기후), electricity (전기), environment (환경, 자연).
Go through about six, new ones first: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and let the learner say it. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: recycling (재활용) — "Recycling isn’t enough."; reduce (줄이다) — "reduce waste"; environmental (환경의) — "an environmental group"; waste (쓰레기(앞에서는 ‘낭비’)) — "food waste"; packaging (포장(재)) — "too much packaging"; ban (금지(규정)) — "a ban on plastic bags"; realistic (현실적인) — "a realistic plan"; habit (습관) — "a good habit"; responsibility (책임) — "It’s our responsibility.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: What’s one thing people around you should cut down on?
I think we should cut down on ___.
Is it realistic to stop using plastic? Why or why not?
It’s not realistic to ___, but we can ___.
What small change could make a difference in your neighborhood?
Small changes like ___ can make a difference.
Who should take more responsibility, people or companies?
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "What’s one thing people around you should cut down on?" (hint on screen: I think we should cut down on ___.)
- "Is it realistic to stop using plastic? Why or why not?" (hint on screen: It’s not realistic to ___, but we can ___.)
- "What small change could make a difference in your neighborhood?" (hint on screen: Small changes like ___ can make a difference.)
- "Who should take more responsibility, people or companies?" (hint on screen: I think ___ should ___, because ___.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.
questions: What’s one thing people around you should cut down on?
Is it realistic to stop using plastic? Why or why not?

Who should take more responsibility, people or companies?

steps.title: The Mug Shelf
steps.text: After the meeting, the café owner joined the group. She had *come across* a simple idea: a shelf of clean mugs beneath the counter for anyone who forgot a cup. “I can’t tackle climate change alone,” she said, “but I can cut down on my own waste.” One neighbor wanted more awareness of energy, too. “We should *take account of* electricity. Does it come from coal or solar power? That’s part of our carbon footprint.” Another neighbor said a mere discount is *of little* use if people forget. “Maybe an electric dishwasher for the mugs?” someone joked. Daniel smiled. “At first, I thought this topic was too small. But I’ve *come around*.” By the end of the month, the café’s paper-cup use had dropped dramatically.
steps.gloss: come across 우연히 발견하다 · awareness 인식, 관심 · take account of ~을 고려하다 · carbon footprint 탄소 발자국(내 생활로 생기는 온실가스) · of little use 별로 쓸모없는 · come around 생각을 바꾸다
questions: Where does the café keep the clean mugs?
Why do you think Daniel changed his mind?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "The Mug Shelf". Text: "After the meeting, the café owner joined the group. She had come across a simple idea: a shelf of clean mugs beneath the counter for anyone who forgot a cup. “I can’t tackle climate change alone,” she said, “but I can cut down on my own waste.” One neighbor wanted more awareness of energy, too. “We should take account of electricity. Does it come from coal or solar power? That’s part of our carbon footprint.” Another neighbor said a mere discount is of little use if people forget. “Maybe an electric dishwasher for the mugs?” someone joked. Daniel smiled. “At first, I thought this topic was too small. But I’ve come around.” By the end of the month, the café’s paper-cup use had dropped dramatically." Words: come across 우연히 발견하다 · awareness 인식, 관심 · take account of ~을 고려하다 · carbon footprint 탄소 발자국(내 생활로 생기는 온실가스) · of little use 별로 쓸모없는 · come around 생각을 바꾸다.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "Where does the café keep the clean mugs?" / "Why do you think Daniel changed his mind?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘We should cut down on ___.’로 무언가를 줄이자고 제안할 수 있어요.
‘It’s not realistic to ___.’로 지금 하기엔 너무 어려운 생각이라고 말할 수 있어요.
‘Small changes can make a difference.’로 작은 실천을 격려할 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘We should cut down on ___.’로 무언가를 줄이자고 제안할 수 있어요.
- ‘It’s not realistic to ___.’로 지금 하기엔 너무 어려운 생각이라고 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘Small changes can make a difference.’로 작은 실천을 격려할 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, react, say that the next lesson comes next, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.title: 키오스크 시대
steps.title_en: Some people are being left behind.
steps.goal: 편리함과 소외를 함께 보고 대안을 말하기
steps.scene_desc: 11월 중순 저녁, 동네 국숫집 입구의 주문용 키오스크 앞. 나이 든 이웃이 화면 앞에서 손을 멈추고 난처한 표정, 지우가 옆에서 화면을 가리키며 차근차근 도와주고, 벤이 뒤에서 부드럽게 웃으며 지켜봄. 식당 안에는 김이 오르는 국수 그릇(화면·간판·메뉴에 글자 없이)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Some people are being left behind." (키오스크 시대). Goal: 편리함과 소외를 함께 보고 대안을 말하기. Today's scene: 11월 중순 저녁, 동네 국숫집 입구의 주문용 키오스크 앞. 나이 든 이웃이 화면 앞에서 손을 멈추고 난처한 표정, 지우가 옆에서 화면을 가리키며 차근차근 도와주고, 벤이 뒤에서 부드럽게 웃으며 지켜봄. 식당 안에는 김이 오르는 국수 그릇(화면·간판·메뉴에 글자 없이). Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.

steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Not everyone is comfortable with ___. / There should be an option to ___. Table (Not everyone is comfortable with … → There should be an option to …):
- touchscreens. → order at the counter.
- paying by phone. → pay in cash.
- small text. → make the text bigger.
- English-only menus. → choose another language.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.

items: leave behind · be being left behind

Don’t *leave* anyone *behind*. 아무도 뒤처지게 두지 말아요. 
Some people *are being left behind*. 뒤처지고 있는 사람들이 있어요. — 지금 일어나는 일

*comfortable with* kiosks / us*ing* kiosks 키오스크(쓰는 것)가 편한 
an *option to* order 주문할 수 있는 선택지 (+ 동사원형)

Some people are being left behind.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- leave behind · be being left behind: Don’t leave anyone behind. 아무도 뒤처지게 두지 말아요. / Some people are being left behind. 뒤처지고 있는 사람들이 있어요. — 지금 일어나는 일
- comfortable with · an option to: comfortable with kiosks / using kiosks 키오스크(쓰는 것)가 편한 / an option to order 주문할 수 있는 선택지 (+ 동사원형)
Common mistakes on screen:
- Some people are being leave behind. → Some people are being left behind. (과거분사 left를 써요.)
- She isn’t comfortable to kiosks. → She isn’t comfortable with kiosks. (comfortable with + 명사.)
- an option to ordering → an option to order (to 뒤에는 동사원형.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.
points: leave behind · be being left behind: Don’t leave anyone behind. 아무도 뒤처지게 두지 말아요. Some people are being left behind. 뒤처지고 있는 사람들이 있어요. — 지금 일어나는 일
comfortable with · an option to: comfortable with kiosks / using kiosks 키오스크(쓰는 것)가 편한 an option to order 주문할 수 있는 선택지 (+ 동사원형)

She isn’t comfortable to kiosks. → She isn’t comfortable with kiosks.

steps.note: 예) touchscreens / order at the counter → Not everyone is comfortable with touchscreens. There should be an option to …
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) touchscreens / order at the counter → Not everyone is comfortable with touchscreens. There should be an option to …. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: touchscreens → order at the counter | QR codes → get a paper menu | self-checkout → pay a staff member | voice assistants → type instead.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

cards: Some people are being left behind.
There should be an option to ___.
steps.teach:
This is the start of session 2 of "Some people are being left behind." (키오스크 시대); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Not everyone is comfortable with ___." / "Some people are being left behind." / "There should be an option to ___.". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: It’s a sign of the times.
There’s no one to ask for help.
Staff should be there to help.
We should make it easier for everyone.
모두가 더 쉽게 쓸 수 있게 만들어야 해요.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 좋은 점: "Kiosks save businesses money." (가게가 키오스크로 돈을 아껴요., 보통); "Lines move faster." (줄이 더 빨리 줄어요., 보통); "It’s a sign of the times." (시대가 그렇죠., 친근)
- 문제점: "My parents find them confusing." (부모님이 어려워하세요., 보통); "The screens are too small." (화면이 너무 작아요., 보통); "There’s no one to ask for help." (도와 달라고 할 사람이 없어요., 보통)
- 아이디어: "Staff should be there to help." (도와줄 직원이 있어야 해요., 보통); "Design matters." (디자인이 중요해요., 보통); "We should make it easier for everyone." (모두가 더 쉽게 쓸 수 있게 만들어야 해요., 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 더 나은 키오스크 디자인: big-text mode 큰 글씨 모드 / a help button 직원 호출 버튼 / a lower screen 휠체어에서도 손이 닿는 낮은 화면
- (참고) 사회 낱말 더 보기: an immigrant 이민자(다른 나라로 옮겨 와 사는 사람) · immigration 이민 / a refugee 난민(안전을 위해 자기 나라를 떠나야 하는 사람) / illegal 불법의 · jail 교도소 · pray 기도하다
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: My dad isn’t comfortable ___ kiosks. B: Mine either. Some people are being left ___. / A: There should be an ___ to order at the counter. B: Yes. Design ___. / 낱말 상자: with · behind · option · matters
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: kiosk (키오스크, 무인 주문기), touchscreen (터치스크린), self-checkout (셀프 계산대), QR code (QR 코드), voice assistant (음성 비서), drive-thru (드라이브 스루(차에서 주문)), interface ((화면) 인터페이스), barrier (장벽, 걸림돌), accessibility (접근성(누구나 쓰기 쉬움)), inclusive (모두를 포함하는), cost (비용), automatically (자동으로).
Go through about six, new ones first: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and let the learner say it. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: digital (디지털의) — "digital menus"; elderly (연세 드신, 고령의) — "elderly customers"; confusing (헷갈리게 하는, 어려운) — "The menu is confusing."; staff (직원) — "Ask a staff member."; design (디자인, 설계) — "Design matters."; option (선택(지)) — "a cash option"; convenience (편리함) — "the convenience of kiosks"; labor (노동, 일) — "labor costs"; technology (기술) — "new technology"; adapt (적응하다) — "It takes time to adapt.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Where do you see kiosks or self-checkouts most often?
Who might not be comfortable with kiosks? Why?
Not everyone is comfortable with ___, because ___.
What option should every kiosk have?
There should be an option to ___.
Are kiosks a good change overall?
They save ___. At the same time, ___.
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Where do you see kiosks or self-checkouts most often?" (hint on screen: I often see them at ___.)
- "Who might not be comfortable with kiosks? Why?" (hint on screen: Not everyone is comfortable with ___, because ___.)
- "What option should every kiosk have?" (hint on screen: There should be an option to ___.)
- "Are kiosks a good change overall?" (hint on screen: They save ___. At the same time, ___.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: The Last Meeting of the Year
steps.text: At the last discussion group of the year, Jiwoo shared the kiosk story. A neighbor who runs a small shop said the machine helps with labor costs. “But I still keep one person at the counter. That’s *in line with* how I want to treat customers.” Another neighbor had just *moved out* of her parents’ home. “Now they call me every time they order food!” she laughed. Jiwoo suggested a big-text mode and a help button. “That’s *consistent with* inclusive design,” said Daniel. Ben added, “Helping a neighbor is a small way to *give back*.” Then Daniel thanked everyone for a great year. Later, he added, “In December, let’s have dinner at Grace’s place: Grace, Chloe, Maya, Ben, Jiwoo, and me.” Grace smiled. “I’ll cook!”
steps.gloss: in line with ~에 맞는 · move out (살던 집에서) 나가 살다 · consistent with ~와 일치하는 · inclusive 모두를 포함하는 · give back (받은 것을) 돌려주다, 주변에 베풀다

Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "Why does the shop owner keep one person at the counter?" / "Where will the six friends have dinner in December?". steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘Not everyone is comfortable with ___.’로 어떤 변화가 누군가에게는 어렵다고 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘Some people are being left behind.’로 뒤처지는 사람이 있다고 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘There should be an option to ___.’로 필요한 선택지를 제안할 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, react, say that the next lesson comes next, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.
